chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān ibn Muslim, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Anṣār used to work with their water-carrying camels and their property. Then, when Friday came, they would come, and the people were bothered by the odors of their armpits and their bodies. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded them to perform ghusl (ritual bath) on Friday, and thus the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be established by that.

key_terms.أَرْوَاحِ آبَاطِهِمْ: the odors coming from their armpits
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارُ: the Helpers of Madinah among the early Muslims
key_terms.نَوَاضِحِهَا: water-carrying camels used for labor and irrigation
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day of congregational gathering

ai.seo_question: Why was ghusl (ritual bath) on Friday legislated in the Prophetic sunnah (prophetic tradition)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the background for the institution of Friday ghusl (ritual bath). Because people came to the Friday gathering after labor and caused discomfort through bodily odor, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed them to bathe, and this became an established sunnah (prophetic tradition).
